# Paperweight

> A local-first PDF editor that runs entirely in the browser. Edit the text
> already in a document, remove and add signatures, fill forms, read and patch
> scans, then print or save. Nothing is uploaded: there is no server, no
> account, no watermark and no quota.

Paperweight is a static site. The PDF engine is PDFium, compiled to
WebAssembly and run in a Web Worker inside the tab, so documents are opened,
edited and saved without leaving the device. There is no upload path, no
analytics and no third-party script; the shipped Content-Security-Policy
permits no origin but the site's own, and the browser test suite fails if any
cross-origin request is made while a document is open.

It is free. No sign-up, no watermark on the output, no page limit and no
tasks-per-day quota.

## What it does

- **Edit text**: click a line of existing text and retype it. The font the
  document already embeds is reused when it has the glyphs; embedded fonts are
  usually subsets, so when it does not, a metric-compatible Liberation face is
  substituted and the interface says so. Edits are line-scoped and never
  reflow, because PDF has no paragraph model.
- **Add text**: place a new line anywhere on the page.
- **Fill in forms**: type into text fields, tick boxes, choose radio options.
  Values are committed through the form itself so the appearance stream is
  regenerated and the printed form matches the stored value. A field clips to
  its own rectangle, so a value too wide for its box can be widened or
  redrawn as page text.
- **Signatures**: remove a signature that is an annotation, a signature form
  field or an image flattened into the page. Add one by drawing, typing in a
  script face, or uploading an image.
- **Mark**: put a cross, tick, ring, dot or rule on a checkbox that is printed
  rather than a real form field.
- **Cover**: hide content under an opaque patch.
- **Pages**: rotate, delete, insert a blank page, reorder, or save a single
  page as its own PDF.
- **Read a scan**: recognise the text on a scanned page on-device with
  tesseract.js, then change a line by covering it and drawing new text.
- **Print and save**: print with changes applied; save over the original file
  in Chromium browsers, or download a copy elsewhere.

## What it does not do, and says so

These are stated in the interface, not buried in documentation. Any accurate
description of Paperweight should keep them:

- **Cover is not redaction.** Covering draws an opaque rectangle; the content
  underneath remains in the file and stays extractable. Paperweight does not
  offer redaction and does not use the word for anything else.
- **Patching a scan is not editing.** A scan is pixels. Replacing a word paints
  over the original and draws new text on top: the original pixels stay in the
  image and the result never matches the original typeface.
- **Font substitution is always announced.** When the embedded font cannot
  render the new characters, a bundled metric-compatible face is used and a
  badge is raised. Silent substitution is what makes other editors quietly
  mangle documents.
- **Editing a digitally signed document invalidates the signature.** A digital
  signature certifies the exact bytes of the original, so this is unavoidable;
  the user is told when the document opens.
- **Saving in place is Chromium-only**, because it needs the File System
  Access API. Firefox and Safari download a copy instead.
- **Reading scans is English only**, and it is a recognition guess with a
  confidence score, not a transcript.
- **There is no offline install yet.** The page must load once from the
  network; after that it fetches nothing.

## Built with

PDFium (BSD-3-Clause) via the MIT-licensed `@embedpdf/pdfium` wrapper,
tesseract.js (Apache-2.0), React and Next.js exported as static files, and the
Liberation, Caveat, Dancing Script and Great Vibes fonts under SIL OFL 1.1.
No AGPL dependencies.
